You're being asked to plan for growth that hasn't happened yet.

The pipeline looks promising, but decisions about resources, priorities, and future goals can't always wait until every opportunity closes. Understanding what's behind the numbers matters.

My Business Development Performance Power BI Kit helps you examine pipeline health and opportunity details: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595453904/power-bi-business-development-dashboard

A strong business development pipeline can still leave plenty of uncertainty about future growth.

Total open value shows potential business, while weighted pipeline adds estimated win probabilities. Neither guarantees what will actually close, but the comparison can help clarify the assumptions behind a plan.

Try reviewing both values before your next planning meeting. Identify the opportunities contributing most to the difference.

Growth planning often requires decisions before the outcomes are known.

Leaders may need to discuss staffing, priorities, and resources while important opportunities are still open. A clearer understanding of pipeline stages, probability, and opportunity mix can make those conversations more informed.

My Business Development Performance Power BI Kit provides three editable reporting views: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595453904/power-bi-business-development-dashboard

Before making plans around future business, it's worth examining the assumptions behind your pipeline.

A large opportunity may have a low win probability, an uncertain close date, or dependencies that deserve attention. Those details can change how confidently you interpret the total.

Try reviewing your five largest open opportunities. Record their stages, estimated probabilities, expected close dates, and the assumptions most worth validating.

You don't need perfect predictions to make thoughtful business development decisions.

Understanding pipeline value, win probability, opportunity stages, and team goals can help identify uncertainties worth discussing. That context supports planning for different possibilities without pretending the future is settled.

Planning for future growth can be uncomfortable when so much depends on opportunities that haven't closed.

Business development leaders still have to consider resources, priorities, and goals while acknowledging uncertainty. Pipeline reporting can help clarify the assumptions, but judgment remains essential.
